# GUI owner policy binding — source review

## Contents

1. [Scope and status](#scope-and-status)
2. [Producer and consumer trace](#producer-and-consumer-trace)
3. [Correction and compatibility](#correction-and-compatibility)
4. [Invariants and regression plan](#invariants-and-regression-plan)
5. [Original-body negative control](#original-body-negative-control)
6. [Own review and residual work](#own-review-and-residual-work)

## Scope and status

The source input is pull request (PR) #663 at
`c7617d1027888271a83c3b724171e1363289995e`; the stated master input is
`75dbc6406123e22468f168b861d5e0622c9d5769`. The isolated editable source is
`architecture/source` under this evidence directory. The repository objects
were used read-only for original-source comparisons.

The canonical instructions read were `metadata/AGENTS.md`, followed by the
relevant PR verification, graphical user interface (GUI), supervisor state,
and managed-upgrade sections of `metadata/agent-runbook.md`. The latter was
provided from the current instructions branch because it is absent from the
#663 tree. Applied skills: Architecture Review, Ponytail, and Go Testing and
Verification.

**This is a source-only review.** No Go compiler, formatter, test binary,
native Product, remote execution, external reviewer, installation, workflow
dispatch, or Git publication was run by this implementation agent. The parent
agent owns qualified execution, physical architecture scans, and any separately
authorized publication. Test results below are expected oracles, not receipts.

Table 1. Changed source inventory.

| Path | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_lifecycle.go` | Narrow retained policy dependency, one compatibility construction, exact-record binding after successful publication, and policy use during handoff. |
| `internal/gui/single_instance.go` | Carry the optional policy through both acquisition branches; return the same acquisition-bound lifecycle; preserve standalone write defaults. |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_lifecycle_test.go` | Adapt two existing direct fixtures to explicit policy arguments; guarantee release of the fixture lock on early failures in the bound-lifecycle regression. |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_policy_test.go` | Three semantic regressions, 14 leaf subtests, sealed filesystem fixtures, and policy-return fault injection. |

No architecture policy, baseline, worker registry, GUI Server, command-line
interface (CLI), application programming interface (API) implementation,
frontend, or dependency files were edited.

## Producer and consumer trace

1. The ordinary command in `internal/cli/gui.go` optionally captures the
   complete resume-policy preimage, then calls `acquireSingleInstanceWithHandoff`.
   That reaches `gui.AcquireSingleInstanceAt` before the ordinary Server is
   constructed. It is therefore incorrect to require `Server.api` for owner
   publication.
2. The ordinary legacy path takes the adjacent `.lock` file through
   `tryAcquireSingleInstanceLockAt`. The reservation-aware path takes the same
   file lock, validates the handoff marker and deadline, and admits only the
   designated child while a reservation is open. Rejected marker/reservation
   observations return through the existing tentative-lease release paths.
3. Only after acquisition and any reservation checks does either path create
   `GUIOwnerLifecycle`, binding its `GUIOwnerPolicy` once. With an explicit
   resume, `ResumeGUIOwner` must complete, including its settings-lock release.
   `WithGUIOwnerControl` then validates automatic start and must also complete
   its release before any active GUI-owner record is written.
4. `internal/api/gui_owner_control.go` delegates these operations to the
   existing settings transaction in `internal/api/settings.go`.
   `mutateSettingsMapLockedThen` owns the in-process mutex plus the settings
   file lock. Its deferred `releaseAndJoinApplied` preserves release failures,
   including an already-applied resume. The caller therefore must test the
   returned error, not only successful callback execution or `Applied`.
5. `currentGUIOwnerRecord` reads the current process generation; the
   hardened state writer publishes the version-two record. `publishCurrent`
   binds that exact successful record to the lifecycle without a second read.
   A failed resume, settings read, policy decision, release, identity read, or
   durable write never exposes the new lifecycle to the caller.
6. `SingleInstanceLock.OwnerLifecycle` carries that object through
   `releaseOnceLease` and `ownerLifecycleFromLease`. Ordinary
   `startGuiServerWithStartup` obtains it before constructing the Server.
   The ready path updates its bound port; deferred shutdown terminally settles
   its generation before releasing the GUI lease.
7. The structured restart-child branch is different from ordinary startup:
   `runRestartV3ChildStartup` creates a Server and binds an authenticated standby
   listener before the child acquires the GUI lease. The child still obtains
   the durable owner exclusively through `SpawnedGUIChild.AcquireSingleInstanceAt`,
   then passes the acquisition-bound lifecycle into runtime startup. The
   corrected policy binding does not depend on that Server existing either.
8. `buildRestartV3ParentDependencies` obtains `OwnerLifecycle` from the lease.
   `RestartCoordinator` reserves its child, then invokes `BeginHandoff` before
   releasing the parent lease. `BeginHandoff` first checks the same process ID
   (PID), creation time, generation, and active state; only then does it query
   the retained policy and write the handoff record. Its policy dependency is
   no longer reconstructed inside the transition.
9. `KillRecordedHolder` eventually reacquires through `AcquireSingleInstanceAt`
   after its existing native settlement protocol. That producer receives the
   same default owner binding. No native kill or takeover code was changed or
   exercised by these new tests.

`AcquireSingleInstanceLockOnlyAt`, absent-owner handling, compare-and-swap
generation checks, rollback, terminal settlement, and reservation validation
remain with their existing owners. The correction introduces no process or
settings ownership outside this chain.

## Correction and compatibility

`GUIOwnerPolicy` has only the two settings operations already used by this
lifecycle. `SingleInstanceAcquireOptions.OwnerPolicy` allows a composition to
supply that authority. The chosen reference is held in the lifecycle, so
changing the caller's later composition cannot silently redirect a transition.
The dependency's policy observations remain fresh; its binding is retained,
not its settings values.

For existing callers that supply no policy, `newGUIOwnerLifecycle` creates one
API handle. This default is used by ordinary acquisition, reservation-aware
acquisition, `NewGUIOwnerLifecycle`, and `WritePidport`. `NewAPI` itself starts
no background resource according to the inspected `internal/api/api.go`;
these policy methods operate on the existing canonical settings store. The
change therefore claims explicit dependency lifetime and testability, not a
proved production resource leak in the old code.

Public function signatures, no-option acquisition, conditional resume, error
classification, handoff-reservation behavior, legacy record reading, and the
durable record format remain compatible. The private legacy acquisition helper
now accepts the existing options type so it can retain the policy as well as
the resume preimage. All inspected composite options literals are keyed.

`publishCurrent` is responsible for the write-to-binding boundary: it records
identity only after the durable write succeeds and prevents the two acquisition
branches from duplicating that state transfer. It is used before a newly
created lifecycle is exposed and adds no post-publication file read.

The default `api.NewAPI()` call is still outside `internal/app`. This is an
explicit compatibility construction at an owner-creation boundary, not a claim
that the repository has completed composition-root migration. No global
factory, production test hook, new service layer, or alternate settings store
was added.

## Invariants and regression plan

Table 2. New semantic oracles.

| Top-level test | Leaf subtests | Observable property |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestGUIOwnerPolicyAcquisitionKeepsIndependentOwners` | `legacy`, `reservation` | An explicit resume clears only the first injected policy's stop attribution and preserves its autorun preference. Both owners publish version-two records. A later stop in A refuses A's handoff without changing its record; B independently writes a handoff with its original process generation. Publication remains outside both policy-return boundaries while the original GUI lease stays held. |
| `TestGUIOwnerPolicyAcquisitionRefusalPreservesRecord` | Each of `legacy`, `reservation`, with `resume_conflict`, `resume_release`, `policy_read`, `stopped`, `policy_release` | Refusal preserves the prior tombstone byte for byte, returns the specific error, exposes no owner, and releases the tentative GUI lease. An applied resume followed by release failure still refuses publication; no later admission runs after a resume error. |
| `TestGUIOwnerPolicyHandoffRefusalPreservesRecord` | `policy_read`, `policy_release` | A failure before or after the policy callback preserves the active record byte for byte and keeps the original owner lease. |

The green run has **3 top-level tests, 14 leaves, and 2 intermediate route
subtests: 19 test/subtest terminal events plus one package terminal event**.
There must be no skipped or missing required terminals. A focused selector is:

```text
^TestGUIOwnerPolicy(AcquisitionKeepsIndependentOwners|AcquisitionRefusalPreservesRecord|HandoffRefusalPreservesRecord)$
```

Relevant existing regressions include all seven roots in
`gui_owner_lifecycle_test.go`, first/second single-instance acquisition,
`TestWritePidport_WritesBothPidAndPort`, and the reservation-gate regressions.
Their exact runnable set must be separately admitted by the qualification
owner; selecting the entire GUI package can reach native subprocess tests.

### Fixture and assertion boundaries

- Each new test explicitly seals `LOCALAPPDATA` to `apitest.HardenedTempDir`,
  including the canonical API fallback reached by the negative control.
  Normal GUI `TestMain` additionally redirects state and client paths.
- The two independent policies are injected fixtures. They demonstrate
  per-owner dependency binding; they do not imply separate persisted settings
  stores for default production owners.
- Real file locks and owner records exist only inside fixture directories.
  The only native process observation is the executing test process's own
  identity. Synthetic prior PID 42 and target child PIDs are record data only;
  the tests neither probe nor signal those processes.
- `processIDWindows` and its command-line query close their query handles;
  `currentGUIOwnerRecord` does not request the separate retained-process probe.
- Settings-release failures are modeled at the interface's synchronous return
  boundary; they are not native operating-system unlock-failure qualification.
  Real GUI lease ownership and durable-file ordering are observed at that
  boundary.
- Callback assertions use nonfatal errors, permitting acquisition to return
  and release its tentative lease on an observed regression. Successful or
  unexpectedly returned leases immediately register terminal settlement and
  `ReleaseErr` cleanup before temporary-directory removal.
- There are no new goroutines, timers, native listeners, subprocess launches,
  process termination, scheduler mutation, or parallel tests. The reservation
  branch uses the existing deterministic clock and marker-reader fixtures.

## Original-body negative control

Use a separate candidate copy. Keep the candidate types, signatures,
acquisition plumbing, and all test files. Restore the **exact original body
bytes** from `c7617d1027888271a83c3b724171e1363289995e` for:

1. `writeCurrentGUIOwnerRecord`;
2. `(*GUIOwnerLifecycle).BeginHandoff`.

The first signature retains its new `policy` parameter, which the restored
body legitimately ignores. Go permits unused parameters. No test oracle or
fixture is changed. The complete behavior-reversion diff is equivalent to:

```diff
-        if _, err := policy.ResumeGUIOwner(*resume[0]); err != nil {
+        if _, err := api.NewAPI().ResumeGUIOwner(*resume[0]); err != nil {
-    if err := policy.WithGUIOwnerControl(func(control api.GUIOwnerControl) error {
+    if err := api.NewAPI().WithGUIOwnerControl(func(control api.GUIOwnerControl) error {
-    if err := l.policy.WithGUIOwnerControl(func(control api.GUIOwnerControl) error {
+    if err := api.NewAPI().WithGUIOwnerControl(func(control api.GUIOwnerControl) error {
```

The bodies become byte-identical to the originals; the surrounding program is
the candidate harness. Label this **original-body behavior reversion**, not an
execution of the unchanged original repository. A build failure would not
establish the intended semantic negative result.

With both bodies restored, the predicted terminal set is:

- **PASS:** only
  `TestGUIOwnerPolicyAcquisitionRefusalPreservesRecord/legacy/resume_conflict`
  and its `reservation/resume_conflict` counterpart. The canonical running
  policy independently rejects those stopped preimages.
- **FAIL:** every other leaf; both intermediate route groups; all three
  top-level tests. Expected total: **17 FAIL and 2 PASS test/subtest terminals,
  plus package FAIL**.

Independent-owner tests fail because the real fallback cannot perform the
fixture's stopped-to-running resume. The other admission refusal leaves either
publish an owner despite the injected failure or return the wrong resume
error. Handoff failure leaves ignore the injected failure and mutate the
active record. The canonical fallback is sealed to test state throughout.

Compile and run both the candidate and this control through the parent-owned
qualified runner. This implementation agent has not executed either. Restore
and verify candidate bytes before any green rerun or publication.

## Own review and residual work

Own full-diff review checked requirements, compatibility, lock ordering,
error propagation, generation binding, callback timing, source scope, and
cleanup. Every changed helper call was searched across the source. No
outstanding source defect was identified by this review; compilation and
execution remain unverified here.

An adjacent test-fixture defect was confirmed during qualification review:
`TestAcquireSingleInstance_BoundLifecycleAvoidsPostPublishOpenFailure` could
call `t.Fatal` after acquiring its fixture flock but before explicit release.
An immediate idempotent `t.Cleanup` with `ReleaseErr` now closes that failure
path. The original successful settlement assertions remain.

The prior triage lists these two GUI-owner findings as **New**, not accepted
baseline entries:

| Original symbol | Fingerprint | Original calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*GUIOwnerLifecycle.BeginHandoff` | `67fadbcd883d0d924e4dbfe27eed665f93a43324c34b6157193f1e3e4f27a946` | 1 |
| `writeCurrentGUIOwnerRecord` | `aeeedf971877511aba0b3bd41dea8eb6024712e9cb0f8efa331a2c9305036b74` | 2 |

The candidate removes those transition-site constructions and introduces one
owner-constructor site in `newGUIOwnerLifecycle`. The physical scan must
establish its actual fingerprint and the before/after deltas. **There is no
baseline-edit candidate unless that scan proves an accepted block disappeared.**
The implementation left `architecture/baseline.yaml` untouched.

Residuals: the compatibility constructor remains outside the future
composition root; full build/vet/test and tagged gates require fresh receipts;
exact-head external review remains separately gated; native GUI restart,
installed-state behavior, and release Product qualification were not exercised.
The wider architecture gate and its previously reported New/Stale/Grown/worker
debt must be recomputed by the parent. This slice establishes no global gate
pass, native lifecycle qualification, or merge permission.

# Independent source review: GUI owner policy binding

## Contents

1. [Verdict and evidence scope](#1-verdict-and-evidence-scope)
2. [Acquisition and consumer trace](#2-acquisition-and-consumer-trace)
3. [Error, nil and compatibility behavior](#3-error-nil-and-compatibility-behavior)
4. [Test review](#4-test-review)
5. [Residuals and unverified claims](#5-residuals-and-unverified-claims)

## 1. Verdict and evidence scope

**No blocking defect identified in the frozen candidate by this independent source review.** Both acquisition branches retain the selected policy before publication, expose the lifecycle only after successful publication, and pass that same object through the inspected existing consumers. Returned policy and settings-release errors prevent publication, and the existing tentative GUI-lease release/error owner remains intact.

This review supplements the implementation owner's review and the root's own review. It is not the separately required external review, a native qualification, or a claim that compilation or tests passed. No source was edited and no Go command, formatter, test binary, remote execution, installation, publication or merge was run.

The comparison baseline is the complete commit `c7617d1027888271a83c3b724171e1363289995e` for pull request (PR) #663. The short prefix `c761` is ambiguous in the local object database; all comparisons used the complete identity. I read `architecture/review.md` and independently compared all extracted source files with that exact Git tree. There are three modified files, one added file and no missing files. Of the four changed files, two are production and two are test files.

**Table 1. Reviewed frozen bytes, before formatting.**

| Path under `architecture/source/` | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_lifecycle.go` | `8cebc4cdeafd71eb556fc0b69c67ae9b2b8b9e7a541f69cea52747363bfe430c` |
| `internal/gui/single_instance.go` | `315bae47d8d06ff00edcb2e23a2403764a4156d2bf358796f5efbe79aba7c702` |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_lifecycle_test.go` | `921d1ea88ae8d77aa4968b1da96f2ec87d4c431c275ae5266647ba8c7cae96ec` |
| `internal/gui/gui_owner_policy_test.go` | `ab5b8e5ed9c6f8d0d53b981ff5b8c9dce7f1aaea26a06e379902a97f3aa44f0d` |

All locations below refer to those bytes. Any later source change requires review of its delta and updated qualification identities.

## 2. Acquisition and consumer trace

### Ordinary acquisition

`internal/gui/single_instance.go:315`, `acquireSingleInstanceAt`, validates option cardinality before taking the file lock. After successful `tryAcquireSingleInstanceLockAt`, it constructs exactly one lifecycle with `option.OwnerPolicy`, calls `publishCurrent`, and attaches the same pointer to `lease.ownerLifecycle` only on success. The new helper does not reconstruct an application programming interface (API) handle inside each transition.

The public dispatcher at `single_instance.go:528` forwards the full options value on the ordinary route. Zero options and `RestartV3Enabled=false` remain valid and do not read a handoff marker. More than one option set remains rejected; the public error classifications are unchanged.

### Reservation-aware acquisition

`single_instance.go:538`, `acquireReservationAwareSingleInstanceAt`, retains the existing sequence: validate the absolute owner-record path, acquire the tentative lock, validate the marker, read the clock, and enforce designated-child/reservation conditions. Only after these checks does it construct the lifecycle with `options.OwnerPolicy` and publish. Rejected reservations therefore do not create an API handle, resume policy, or publish an active record.

Marker/read/clock failures retain their existing `releaseTentativeLeaseUnknown` or `releaseTentativeLeaseWithReason` paths. Publication refusal still calls the same underlying `lease.release` owner and joins its failure with the primary error under `ErrGUIOwnerLeaseUnknown`. The ordinary route uses `ReleaseErr`, which delegates to that same owner. A failed release is not silently translated into a confirmed free lease.

### Publication and retained identity

`gui_owner_lifecycle.go:80`, `newGUIOwnerLifecycle`, selects the supplied policy reference or one default `api.NewAPI()` instance. `publishCurrent` at line 217 passes that stored reference into `writeCurrentGUIOwnerRecord` and copies the returned process generation, process ID (PID) and creation time only after the write succeeds. There is no new post-publication file read.

The helper's mutable identity fields are initialized before the lifecycle is attached to a returned lease. The inspected call graph contains no call to `publishCurrent` on an already-exposed lifecycle. Existing later transitions retain their mutex and generation comparisons; no new goroutine, lock ordering or shared mutable global was introduced.

`BeginHandoff` at `gui_owner_lifecycle.go:279` first reads and matches the active record against the bound PID, creation time and generation. It then queries the retained policy and writes the handoff only after that query returns successfully. The policy is queried again at transition time; the candidate binds the authority reference, not a stale snapshot of its settings values.

## 5. Residuals and unverified claims

These are boundaries or future-provider requirements, not observed blocking defects in the current candidate:

1. **Injected implementations remain trusted dependencies.** `GUIOwnerPolicy` at line 63 does not dynamically validate typed-nil implementations, prevent provider panics/reentrancy, or require callback invocation in code. The default nil-interface case is handled; an arbitrary typed-nil custom provider is not. Current production callers supply the default API, and the new fixtures supply valid objects. A future provider must preserve the synchronous callback/release contract.
2. **Handoff relies on the provider returning a valid decoded control.** At `BeginHandoff:292`, the callback rejects `GUIRunStopped`; it does not independently reject every invalid `RunDesired` value. The default API validates controls before invoking the callback. If a future custom provider supplies a malformed observation with a nil error, it could permit handoff; no current production provider does so. Acquisition separately uses `ValidateAutomaticStart` and rejects an invalid run state. This provider-contract limitation should not be presented as validation of arbitrary implementations.
3. **The default binds an API object, not a frozen filesystem namespace.** `api.WithGUIOwnerControl` and `ResumeGUIOwner` resolve `SettingsPath()` when called. The candidate retains dependency identity and reads fresh values; it does not pin the environment-derived settings path against later process-environment changes. That default behavior is unchanged.
4. **Settings-release errors are simulated at the interface boundary.** The tests prove that the consumer honors returned errors and observes the GUI lease/file ordering. They do not qualify native settings unlock failures, operating-system persistence, process crashes or background GUI restart.
5. **The new reservation-route cases use an empty marker.** They exercise the reservation-aware acquisition branch and its policy plumbing. Nonempty reservations, designated-child authentication and marker/clock refusal remain covered only by separately selected existing tests and source analysis; they were not executed here.
6. **Durable-writer outcome semantics are unchanged.** A successful write is the binding point; no lifecycle is exposed after a returned write error. This review does not prove that every underlying write error implies the file was physically unmodified. Applied-but-unconfirmed storage failures remain the existing state writer's contract and need their own evidence.
7. **Architecture qualification is still pending.** The default `api.NewAPI()` construction has moved to the lifecycle constructor outside the eventual application composition root. No architecture baseline, policy or worker-registry file changed. Physical scans, the exact-head architecture delta, full build/vet/test gates, native Product behavior and external review are outside this source-only verdict.

No corrective edit is requested by this independent review before the root proceeds to its separately authorized formatting, composition admission and focused verification. Any failing execution result must be assessed on its actual cause rather than overridden by this source verdict.
